purpose: The single standard approach EVERY AI — Claude or any other provider — must follow when using the Polari MCP server to inspect and manipulate no-code logic, displays, connectors, topology, and application navigation. Written in JSON so it is both machine-consumable by the AI and human-analyzable: a person can read this file, and the provenance log, to see exactly how an AI is changing Polari's interfaces.
why_json: All interface manipulation flows through typed JSON proposals and a JSON-lines audit log. A reviewer never has to guess what the AI did: every proposed and executed change is a JSON object naming the operation, the authority level, the exact request sent to Polari, and the outcome.
principles: The AI proposes; a deterministic kernel disposes. The model emits a typed proposal; the server's authority kernel classifies and gates it. The model cannot raise its own authority.
No side effect without confirmation. Every mutation is two-step: a propose_* tool returns a dry-run proposal, and nothing changes until polari_execute_proposal(proposal_id, confirm=true).
Incremental over wholesale. Change displays and no-code one reviewable patch at a time, not by replacing whole definitions.
Read before you write. Inspect the current state of a display / solution / simulation before proposing a change to it, and reference the real ids you read.
Everything is auditable. Every proposal and execution is appended to logs/provenance.jsonl as one JSON object per line.
Target by id, never by ambiguous query. Attribute queries can resolve to many instances; mutations address a single id.

authority_ladder.2: reversible-workspace (create scratch instance, step a simulation)
authority_ladder.3: reversible-system (update config, wire a display, add a connector)
authority_ladder.7: irreversible (delete, destructive migration — out-of-band approval required)

auto_execute_threshold: Levels <= POLARI_AUTO_MAX_LEVEL (default 3) execute once confirm=true is passed. Higher levels are refused unless an out-of-band grant (POLARI_ALLOW_HIGH_AUTHORITY) is active. The AI can never self-approve above the threshold.

propose_returns.summary: one line a human can read to understand the intent
propose_returns.request: the exact payload that will be sent to Polari (fully human-analyzable)

mutation_protocol.execute: polari_execute_proposal(proposal_id, confirm=true) — applies the proposal iff the gate allows it; records the outcome to provenance.

topology_awareness.intent: Know the modules, nodes, connections, and shape of the running Polari instance before acting.

nocode_playthrough.intent: Detect the no-code context and play a scenario through it, analyzing the state at each step.
nocode_playthrough.pattern: list runs -> read current-state -> propose a step -> confirm -> read current-state again -> compare. The state before/after each step is the play-through record.

connectors.intent: Wire connectors between no-code / service elements.
connectors.note: Creates a ServiceConnection (or coupling) linking two elements; reversible-system (level 3).

displays.intent: Make displays functional and reactive: inspect them, patch them incrementally, and bind events so they react to state.
displays.pattern: get_display(id) -> propose_display_update(id, patch) with only the fields that change -> confirm. To make a display react to state, propose_bind_event(id, event_spec) wiring a data/equation source or event to the display config.

navigation.intent: Assist a human moving through the application by reporting what exists and where, using ids and class names the UI understands.
navigation.note: Navigation is read/advice (level 0-1): report locations and ids; never mutate to 'navigate'.

political_scorecard.intent: Help a person understand and navigate the scorecard: scoring structure and contexts, policies, judicial/decision context, groups and their authority, data sources, and geographic/map context — then score the issues they care about and refine data against policy.
political_scorecard.pattern: overview -> search for the issue -> read the relevant scoring/policy/source -> propose a score assertion or a pull-and-assert-against-policy -> confirm. Start with polari_psc_overview to orient; use polari_psc_search to jump to an issue the user cares about.

object_storage.intent: Access files in object storage (MinIO) and the managed-file layer.
object_storage.note: Connecting storage is level 4 (network-service) — the AI cannot self-approve it; credentials come from a human.

reasoning_providers.intent: Automate selecting and validating the reasoning provider (null / anthropic / openai / any OpenAI-compatible local or hosted endpoint). Detection reports what each provider needs to be ready.
reasoning_providers.note: The AI may read status, propose a selection (level 3), and validate — but MUST NOT set credentials. Secrets are entered by a human directly through the backend (/ai/providers set_auth) so they never enter an AI tool call or the provenance log. Secrets are stored git-ignored (chmod 600) and never returned by any read.

audit.format: one JSON object per line: {phase, proposal_id, operation, authority_level, summary, request, result|error, clock}
audit.human_use: Read this file to review, in order, every interface change an AI proposed and applied.

envelope.status: HTTP status from Polari (or null on connection failure)

output_contract.note: All tool results are JSON envelopes; mutating tools add operation, authority_level, and proposal_id so a human can trace intent -> gate -> outcome.
